dispositions.inline: Execution of an inline Python program; the member identifies inputs, outputs and enclosing condition. Body and shell continuation belong to the same invocation.
dispositions.script: Execution of the named tracked Python file; argument expression and output/error effects are given by the member. Imports and children are separate edges.
dispositions.selection: Shell/PowerShell selects or tests an interpreter; no Python interpreter is executed by this line. The member identifies its actual consumers.

unresolved_boundaries: This ledger binds reviewed individual candidate IDs only. The checker reports omitted scoped candidates and fails full --check; no blanket acceptance of 386 scanner rows.

Scanner misses shell continuation and selected interpreter probes: package-native-runtime.sh:192 and verify-native-runtime-package.sh:38 execute $candidate -c on a subsequent line; prepare-llama.sh:246 only runs command -v, not a version probe. CMake find_package(Python3) and add_test COMMAND split the configure requirement and CTest invocation across lines.

Scanner calls printf ... | python3 -c a message-or-output, misses $(python_bin) interpreter calls as mention-or-path, and calls Python heredoc body lines and generated fixture text separate executable candidates. Full shell parsing and remainder line review are required.

Source-selected Python dynamic imports, subprocesses, external binaries and runtime-generated fixture modules need separate script-implementation closure. Immediate tracked targets here are not transitive completion evidence.

Required roots include just ci-validate and platform packaging/smoke; optional roots include manual QA, canary family certification, benchmarks and native rewriter CTest. A script may be reached by both roots; requiredness is per caller, not inferred from file path.
